gloss: passing by each other, missing each other, miscommunication

definitions.explanation: The act of two people or things passing each other going in opposite directions.
A situation where people fail to meet or connect, or where there is a misunderstanding or gap in communication.

examples.japanese: {駅|えき}ですれ{違|ちが}いになった。
examples.english: We passed each other at the station.

examples.japanese: {電話|でんわ}のすれ{違|ちが}いで{連絡|れんらく}が{取|と}れなかった。
examples.english: We kept missing each other's calls and couldn't get in touch.

examples.japanese: {二人|ふたり}の{間|あいだ}にすれ{違|ちが}いが{生|う}まれた。
examples.english: A gap developed between the two of them.

examples.japanese: {気持|きも}ちのすれ{違|ちが}いが{原因|げんいん}で{別|わか}れた。
examples.english: They broke up because of emotional disconnection.

examples.japanese: {長年|ながねん}の{夫婦|ふうふ}でも、すれ{違|ちが}いの{生活|せいかつ}が{続|つづ}くと{心|こころ}が{離|はな}れてしまう。
examples.english: Even long-married couples can drift apart if they keep living separate lives.

notes:
The noun form of the verb すれ{違|ちが}う (to pass by each other). Has both a physical and figurative meaning.

SENSE 1 — PHYSICAL:
Two people or things passing each other going in opposite directions.
- {駅|えき}ですれ{違|ちが}いになった: we just missed each other at the station
- {電話|でんわ}のすれ{違|ちが}い: missing each other's phone calls

SENSE 2 — FIGURATIVE:
Emotional disconnect or miscommunication between people. Very common in relationship contexts.
- {気持|きも}ちのすれ{違|ちが}い: emotional disconnect
- すれ{違|ちが}いの{生活|せいかつ}: ships-in-the-night lifestyle (couple rarely seeing each other)

RELATED WORDS:
- すれ{違|ちが}う: to pass by each other (verb form)
- {行|い}き{違|ちが}い: mix-up, misunderstanding (logistics/communication)
